tasks.title: HANGS General Contracting · FY2026 Equipment and Leases Audit
tasks.description: Audit HANGS General Contracting LP’s construction equipment and leases for the year ended June 30, 2026 from 11 Excel, PDF and Word files: the trial balance, the fixed asset register, the purchase invoices and capital requests, the disposal documents, the hours log, the policy, the rental register, the crane rental agreement, the office lease amendment and the lease schedule. Roll the register forward to the books, vouch every addition and disposal, recompute depreciation, read the hours log and test every rental and the office lease under ASC 842. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine gives no opinion.
tasks.outputs: Two files: formula-linked Excel workpapers with tickmarks and evidence tabs, and a draft findings memo PDF for the CPA with evidence trails and the original files attached
tasks.outputsPath: Outputs/HANGS General Contracting FY2026 Equipment and Leases Audit
tasks.gates: Draft workpapers and findings memo, not reviewed, concluded or signed. Not an audit report and no opinion. Open items stay open. The CPA concludes.
tasks.periodLine: FY2026: equipment and leases at June 30, 2026 · audit procedures and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

lines.text: EQ-3205 was scrapped on February 20, 2026 for no proceeds: fully depreciated, removed at $102,600.00 of cost and accumulated depreciation, no gain or loss. EQ-2740, the crawler crane, 100-ton (2005), was sold on March 16, 2026 to Brightwater Crane & Rigging LLC for $180,000.00, paid to Cinderbrook Bank and applied to the term loan. It is still on the register: the proceeds were credited to accumulated depreciation. Its book value at the sale was $110,612.32, its salvage; the $69,387.68 gain on the sale is unrecorded, and cost and accumulated depreciation are overstated by $553,061.60 and $622,449.28 (SALE-01).

lines.text: No purchase option and no transfer; 36 months is a small part of a crawler crane’s life, and the payments’ present value at 7.10%, $699,392.72, is 51.8% of the crane’s $1,350,000.00 value: an operating lease. At June 30, 2026, after 10 payments, the lease liability and the right-of-use asset are $519,770.65. The rent is level, so the year’s expense is right; the balance sheet is missing both (LEASE-02).

lines.text: The office lease’s new term, January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030, is an operating lease that is not recognized. Its rent rises 3% each January, $32,000.00 to $36,016.28 a month. At June 30, 2026 the lease liability is $1,580,613.31 and the right-of-use asset $1,568,742.50. The controller’s schedule used $32,000.00 for all 54 months left and disclosed $1,484,173.90, $96,439.41 short. lines.text: In income the known misstatements nearly offset: the $69,387.68 unrecorded gain against $40,808.04 of capitalized repair, $23,343.96 of depreciation and $11,870.81 of rent, a net ($6,635.13). The balance sheet is another matter: $2,100,383.96 of lease liabilities is missing, 618% of materiality, and the sold crane overstates cost by $553,061.60. The FY2026 covenant procedures read the lease note’s $1,484,173.90 (their DEF-01); this audit finds $2,100,383.96. The CPA weighs these with the other FY2026 areas. The machine stops here.

events.locator: PDF page 1; the Westgate crane rental agreement’s term, rent, equipment and conditions

events.result: No purchase option and no transfer; 36 months is a small part of a crawler crane’s life, and the payments’ present value at 7.10%, $699,392.72, is 51.8% of the crane’s $1,350,000.00 value: an operating lease. At June 30, 2026, after 10 payments, the lease liability and the right-of-use asset are $519,770.65. The rent is level, so the year’s expense is right; the balance sheet is missing both (LEASE-02).

events.locator: Register!A8:Q33, Additions!A8:G15 and Other Entries!A8:D9; every asset’s cost and accumulated depreciation, the additions and the other entries

events.result: In income the known misstatements nearly offset: the $69,387.68 unrecorded gain against $40,808.04 of capitalized repair, $23,343.96 of depreciation and $11,870.81 of rent, a net ($6,635.13). The balance sheet is another matter: $2,100,383.96 of lease liabilities is missing, 618% of materiality, and the sold crane overstates cost by $553,061.60. The FY2026 covenant procedures read the lease note’s $1,484,173.90 (their DEF-01); this audit finds $2,100,383.96. The CPA weighs these with the other FY2026 areas. The machine stops here.
